title: Retraction Watch Database / Crossref: correction and retraction metadata as post-publication memory
summary: The Retraction Watch Database is encoded as post-publication correction-memory infrastructure: it does not reveal the unpublished file drawer, but it makes retractions and some other notices queryable after publication and machine-linkable through Crossref.

status_history.note: Promoted in rev0008 as a denominator-visibility / registration-correction infrastructure record.

claims.claim: Crossref says it acquired the Retraction Watch Database in September 2023, made it publicly available, and that the database contains retractions gathered from publisher websites and updated every working day by Retraction Watch; other notices such as expressions of concern and corrections are included but less comprehensive.
what_would_change_status: Crossref changes ownership/access/update process or database scope.

evidence_migration.note: rev0016 removes overloaded source_support.source_id/record_id keys and uses typed evidence_refs with ref_kind and support_role.

claims.claim: Crossref documentation describes access to Retraction Watch data through the Crossref REST API or full CSV dataset from a Git repository, updated once per working day.
what_would_change_status: Crossref changes API, CSV/Git, or update access model.

claims.claim: Retraction Watch Database User Guide lists searchable fields including author, title, journal, publisher, affiliations, countries, article types, original paper date ranges, notice date ranges, PMID, and DOI.
what_would_change_status: Retraction Watch changes search criteria or database field structure.

evidence_profile.source_depth: one-pass official/institutional HTML extraction; no compliance audit, outcome evaluation, or database sampling yet
limitations: This record establishes infrastructure existence, stated purpose, process fields, and design tradeoffs; it does not estimate coverage, compliance, publication bias reduction, or outcome effects.
Registry presence is not evidence that a study was completed, well conducted, published, unpublished, null, or reported without discrepancies.

type_payload.jurisdiction_or_scope: published scholarly record; Crossref/RW database access and metadata ingestion
signal_capture_model: corrections and expressions of concern where included
reporter_protection_design: not a reporter-protection system; metadata points to public notices and should not be converted into unsourced misconduct claims
limitations: retraction notice reasons require careful interpretation
metadata is not a full causal investigation
type_payload.query_value: Lets the cube track when a published claim was formally modified, retracted, corrected, or placed under concern, and join that to claim-status history.

handling_notes: Registries and post-publication platforms can make hidden or corrected research visible; they can also become instruments of reputational harm if treated as accusation surfaces.
Keep source, claim, study, result, correction, and comment separate. A platform record is not a verdict on any individual study or author.
Private, embargoed, or confidential records must not be bypassed; cite only public source metadata or ethically/lawfully available material.

unknowns: No database sampling was performed in rev0008.
Compliance, result-posting rates, selective public release, correction latency, and field-specific uptake remain open.
No individual trial, preregistration, Registered Report, retraction, or PubPeer thread record is promoted in this revision.
next_actions: Create a study-lifecycle record linking one public preregistration/registry record to its results, publication, and correction/update state.
Add compliance and coverage audits before treating any infrastructure as denominator-complete.
Add negative controls: registered studies whose records did not lead to public results, and public corrections that did not change practice.
